title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Secure Adoption & Governance
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (secure Copilot rollout spanning data readiness/oversharing remediation, sensitivity labels, DLP, access controls, and AI governance; multi-service, higher data-exposure risk).
hook: Roll out Microsoft 365 Copilot without turning oversharing into a data breach
problem: Microsoft 365 Copilot is only as safe as the data it can see — and it can see everything the user can. Turn it on before you've fixed oversharing, missing sensitivity labels, and weak access controls and it will happily surface confidential files, HR data, and stale content to anyone who asks. This solution gives you a repeatable way to adopt Microsoft 365 Copilot securely: assess and remediate oversharing, apply sensitivity labels and DLP so Copilot respects them, tighten access, and put AI governance and a phased rollout in place before you scale.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — how Copilot accesses M365 data (the user's permissions + semantic index), the oversharing risk, how sensitivity labels and DLP constrain Copilot, the access-control and AI-governance model, and the phased adoption approach.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Copilot licensing, Microsoft 365 + Purview, Entra ID, SharePoint/OneDrive access review, sensitivity labels, a pilot group, governance owners) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: assess oversharing and access, remediate (restrict sharing, apply labels, clean up), configure DLP and label-based protections Copilot honors, set AI-governance guardrails and acceptable-use, pilot with a controlled group, validate, then expand.

5 PowerShell scripts — Copilot-readiness + oversharing discovery, per-scope access/label validation, a data-exposure and readiness report, safe remediation of oversharing, and a Copilot pilot scope-group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: A repeatable way to adopt Microsoft 365 Copilot securely — remediate oversharing, apply sensitivity labels and DLP so Copilot respects them, tighten access, and put AI governance and a phased rollout in place. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
